hook: Mirroring a vision transformer's position code alone flips left-right answers in 84-93% of tests.
summary: In three open vision-language models, flipping only the width position code of the image encoder reproduces the answer to a flipped image on most left-right questions in CV-Bench. Mirroring the language model's token positions changes few answers. Results come from three model families and two benchmarks, and the abstract notes that some analyses were run after the fact.
title: Where Do Vision-Language Models Get Left and Right? Position-Code Counterfactuals in Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL and InternVL3
